name: Mattaniah
overview: Mattaniah was a male Levite known as the son of Mica, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 9:15 and Nehemiah 12:8. His identity as a Levite places him within the tribe set apart for service to God, emphasizing his role in the religious life of Israel. Beyond his lineage, there are no additional personal notes recorded.
namesAndTitles: The name Mattaniah means 'gift of YHWH,' reflecting a theologically rich designation that highlights God's gracious provision. This proper name is noted in 1 Chronicles 9:15, though it was not given directly by God but carries a significant meaning consistent with the Levite heritage.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Mattaniah as the son of Mica (1 Chronicles 9:15). Inferred relationships suggest that Jeiel (2 Chronicles 20:14) and Hashabiah (Nehemiah 11:22) may have been his fathers, indicating possible generational connections within the Levitical line. These relationships underscore his place within a family dedicated to temple service.
scriptureSignificance: Mattaniah's significance lies in his Levitical heritage and his role within the post-exilic community, as his lineage is carefully preserved in the biblical record. Being a Levite and son of Mica associates him with the priestly and temple duties critical to Israel's worship and covenant faithfulness. His mention in multiple books reflects the continuity of God's faithful servants through generations, pointing ultimately to the importance of faithful service in God's redemptive plan.
